thread:
deploy-bot: Promotion failed for canary 'redwood-service@v2026-03-23': artifact checksum mismatch for key=artifacts/redwood-service/v2026-03-23.tar.gz : expected=sha256:abcd1234 got=sha256:abcf0000

maria: ugh, seeing this in the release window. is this a transient upload or corrupted artifact? :grimacing:

jon: stacktrace from the promote job — looks like the upload completed but the final bytes differ. log snippet:
```
[2026-03-23T14:05:12Z] upload complete size=14,892,313 bytes
[2026-03-23T14:05:12Z] calculated sha256=abcf0000
[2026-03-23T14:05:12Z] expected sha256 from index=abcd1234
```

ashley: that size mismatch is suspicious. Could be multipart upload race or a truncated copy. Any S3 errors around that time?

kevin: i pulled the object and ran `sha256sum` locally, matches abcf0000. So remote index and object disagree. maybe the artifact index was updated with the wrong digest (race during publish).

maria: deploy-bot shows canary hold automatically. we have a 1h change window open — do we pin to last-good image or abort the whole promote?

release-manager: recommendation: pin to v2026-03-22 (last good) for the rest of the change window to avoid cascading rollbacks. schedule a post-window remediation to reupload and verify the v2026-03-23 artifact.

jon: +1 for pin. If we rerun upload now, we risk another bad artifact under pressure. we should investigate the publisher job.

ashley: steps to remediate after window:
1) mark current artifact as suspect in the artifact index (add tag suspect=true)
2) re-run publish from CI job with `--verify-only` then `--promote`
3) run a quick canary in staging for 30m before reattempting production promote

kevin: i can look at the publisher logs — seems like the publisher did a multipart finalize while a background dedupe job was rewriting the same key. possible concurrent writer.

sre-oncall: checking infra metrics now. no S3 5xx spike, but there were a few failed multipart completes in eu-west-1 at 14:04. i'll open an incident ticket and link it.

maria: for the immediate release decision: pin to v2026-03-22, annotate release notes with the hold and checksum investigation, and unblock other services. who can trigger the pin?

deploy-bot: Usage: `deploybot pin --service redwood-service --image v2026-03-22 --reason "artifact checksum mismatch v2026-03-23"`

jon: i'll run the pin now. running:
```bash
deploybot pin --service redwood-service --image v2026-03-22 --reason "artifact checksum mismatch v2026-03-23"
```

jon: pinned and promoted. canary points to v2026-03-22 again. :thumbsup:

release-manager: thanks. i'll update the release notes: "Canary promotion for 2026-03-23 held due to artifact checksum mismatch. Rolled back to v2026-03-22 to maintain SLAs. Investigation ongoing."

ashley: opened a follow-up ticket (ARTIFACT-1423) to investigate concurrent publisher/dedupe interaction and to add a post-publish verification step. tagging @kevin and @jon.

kevin: i'll add a guard in the publisher to verify digest after finalize and retry finalize if mismatch detected. also add a quick integration test for concurrent writes.

maria: thanks all. for transparency: we're keeping the change window but blocking this bit until remediation. other unrelated promotes can proceed. please add any further notes to ARTIFACT-1423. :eyes:

sre-oncall: incident created: INC-2026-031 — monitoring multipart finalize errors and throttling concurrent writes. will post updates there.

deploy-bot: Canary promotion status: held -> rolled-back -> stable (pinned v2026-03-22).

release-manager: final: no rollback across services, just a pin for this service. we'll revisit after ARTIFACT-1423 triage next week. closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
